v1.feedback: The Riley op-art grid reads instantly and the phosphorescence cycle is a genuinely clever inversion — dark stripes becoming cyan-green emitters while the background flips to near-black is a satisfying 'lights-out' moment that earns the linked word. Two things to tighten: the twist parameter can roll high enough that the grid loses its structured Riley identity and becomes a generic swirl, so clamp uTwist to ~1.5 rad max; and the glow transition is linear and could benefit from a sharper onset with a slower decay (ease-out curve on uGlow ramp-up, longer exponential tail on fade) to better mimic real phosphorescent afterglow persistence. The white-on-white BW phase is clean but the 2.2px point size feels slightly under-resolved at 1x DPR — consider bumping to 2.8 or scaling with frustum coverage.

v2.feedback: The phosphorescence cycle concept clearly drove the design — sharp onset / slow decay mimics real afterglow well, and the Riley op-art parent is preserved with clamped twist and interference stripes. Main issue: the canvas clearColor stays 0xffffff throughout, which will wash out the cyan-green phosphor glow against white; the background must lerp to near-black (e.g. 0x050505) in sync with uGlow to sell the dark-room afterglow effect. Additionally, the glow activates globally and uniformly — a traveling wave of phosphorescence (e.g. radial sweep or row-by-row ignition keyed to grid position) would add temporal depth and make the 'surprise' moment more cinematic rather than a flat uniform color swap.
